title: SLO-gradient scheduler with tenant-weighted KV eviction
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching on shared GPUs creates contention between tenants. Existing preemptors use coarse priority bands which cause either starving of low-tier customers or excessive KV evictions that harm tail latency. Goal: implement an SLO-aware scheduling layer that dynamically scores inflight and queued requests using an SLO gradient (how close a request/tenant is to SLO breach) and a tenant-weighted eviction mediator that minimizes overall expected latency/regression due to KV evictions. The feature should reduce P99 tail regressions during load spikes while providing transparent tenant weight controls for fairness.

Acceptance criteria:
- New scheduler reduces P99 tail by >= 12% in synthetic multi-tenant spike tests vs current banded preemptor.
- Average KV eviction-induced regens reduced by >= 20% for medium/low-priority tenants.
- No more than 2% increase in median latency for high-priority tenants.
- Metrics instrumented and visible in Console: per-tenant SLO headroom, eviction_rate, preempt_events, reclaimed_gpu_memory.
- Gradual rollout steps and kill-switch implemented.

Background/context: This work is driven by customer incidents during burst events where low-priority requests evict hot KV entries, causing subsequent token-generation slowdowns that push mid-priority customers to SLO violations. Related tickets: ENG-7421 (SLO-aware batching preemption fairness), ENG-17283, ENG-31502. This ticket is intended to implement a complementary algorithm with different trade-offs: shorter preemption reaction time and an eviction cost model that reasons about expected regen cost (tokens remaining * model throughput cost) plus KV hotness.
